motions.title: Confirmation of Minutes 1 August 1995
motions.description: Confirmation of minutes from Special Meeting held on 1 August 1995.

motions.title: Home Occupation at 47 Kalinda Drive, City Beach
motions.description: Application by D D Boyer to operate a management consultancy office from a dwelling, employing the applicant and one other person, using a 12 square metre room with telephone, facsimile and personal computer equipment. No submissions received from adjoining landowners.

motions.title: Home Occupation at 112 Harborne Street, Wembley
motions.description: Application by [private individual — name withheld] to use a portion of an outbuilding (garage) as an office for a desktop publishing business. The proposed office is 14 square metres, operated by the sole proprietor using one computer, fax machine, printer and telephone. Operating hours 8.00 am to 4.30 pm. No objections received from adjoining landowners.

motions.title: Delegated Decisions and Notifications
motions.description: Information report on development approvals and notifications processed under delegated authority for the month ending 31 July 1995, including home occupation renewals and facade refurbishments.

motions.title: Alterations to Side Boundary Setbacks at 17 Lake Monger Drive
motions.description: Application for planning approval for minor amendments to previously approved nine two-storey town houses. Changes include alteration to side setback boundary of unit 5 from 1.4 metres to 1.28 metres (reduction of 120 millimetres) and relocation of storeroom for unit 1 from front courtyard to between garage and boundary. Units already constructed. Variations arose from sewer depth requirements.

motions.title: Proposed Subdivision at 145 Herdsman Parade, Wembley
motions.description: Application to subdivide 2074 square metre lot into two lots: one of 533 square metres for residence and one of 1541 square metres for printing works. Application referred by Western Australian Planning Commission for Council comment and recommendation. Proposal inconsistent with Scheme objectives as existing buildings would not comply with setback and plot ratio requirements for Office/Residential 1 Zone.

motions.title: Four Grouped Dwellings at 368 Cambridge Street, Wembley
motions.description: Application for development of four 2-storey grouped dwellings on 1009 square metre lot. Dwelling to be demolished. Design sympathetic to surroundings with retention of mature Queensland box trees. Proposal complies with Scheme except for minor front setback variation (5.8 metres to buildings vs 6.0 metres required, and 4.5 metres to carports). Discussion raised concerns about style and lack of consultation with neighbouring property owner. Motion moved to defer application for further consideration.

motions.title: Home Occupation at 58 Essex Street, Wembley
motions.description: Application by B M Cornille to use one room of residence (10 square metres) as office and part of garage for storage. Mail order business, sole operator. Equipment: telephone only. Operating hours: 9.00 am to 3.00 pm weekdays maximum. Occasional deliveries (estimated once every two months). One telephone response received with no objection provided no increase in traffic.

motions.title: Draft Planning Policy: Satellite Dishes and Antennae
motions.description: Draft policy for Domestic Satellite Dishes, Microwave Antennae and Tower Masts. Policy establishes criteria for approval and exemptions, addresses visual impact, includes administration requirements including fees and delegated authority provisions. One month public advertising period proposed.

motions.title: Building Licences Approved Under Delegated Authority
motions.description: Schedule of building licences approved under delegated authority for the month of July 1995.

motions.title: Building Licence for Medical Rooms at 160B Cambridge Street
motions.description: Application from Sam Butto, Architects on behalf of [private individual — name withheld] for construction of Medical Rooms (Eye Specialist). Works include one lower level undercraft carport, two procedure rooms, sterilisation room and administration areas on upper level. Project value $380,000. Development Application approved 17 January 1995. Building Licence approval required as project exceeds $175,000.

motions.title: Two Storey Residence at 10 Kavanagh Street, West Leederville
motions.description: Application for two storey residence exceeding Council Policy No 13 plot ratio for R30 area (0.462:1 proposed vs 0.4:1 required). Council previously refused similar application. New application with reduced floor area (17.54 square metres reduction) and increased rear setback (1.6 metres additional). Owners of rear property have approved subject to conditions. Absolute majority required due to non-compliance with plot ratio policy.

motions.title: Proposed Studio at 137 The Boulevard, Floreat
motions.description: Application to construct studio on western side boundary. Studio wall 6.0 metres long, 3.0 metres high, with nil setback (1.0 metre required). Adjoining neighbour objected due to loss of light and amenity. Studio would cover existing glass block panel in neighbour's boundary wall. Proposal recommended for refusal. Discussion noted valid objection from neighbour and deferred for further consideration.

motions.title: Vary Order of Business - Ocean Gardens Retirement Estate
motions.description: Motion to vary order of business to deal with urgent business relating to Ocean Gardens Retirement Estate at 6.08 pm due to attendance of Council's legal representative [private individual — name withheld].

motions.title: Confidential Treatment of Ocean Gardens Matter
motions.description: Motion to treat Ocean Gardens Retirement Estate matter as confidential and conduct meeting behind closed doors due to sensitive nature of the item.

motions.title: Suspend Standing Orders Sub-Clause 3.3.4
motions.description: Motion to suspend operations of Sub-Clause 3.3.4 of the Standing Orders to conduct confidential discussion on Ocean Gardens Retirement Estate matter.

motions.title: Resume Standing Orders and Open Doors
motions.description: Motion to resume operations of Sub-Clause 3.3.4 of the Standing Orders and proceed with open doors following confidential discussion on Ocean Gardens Retirement Estate.

motions.title: Street Parking Monitoring in West Leederville and Wembley
motions.description: Appointment of BSD Consultants to undertake monitoring tasks related to street parking in West Leederville and Wembley at cost of $12,000 (including $1,000 disbursement sum). Tasks include leaflet drop, resident survey, parking surveys during football and non-football events, and analysis report. Monitoring Group established June 1995. Bids received from BSD Consultants ($12,000) and Mitchell McCotter ($15,100).

motions.title: West Coast Highway Environmental Conditions
motions.description: Progress report on environmental conditions associated with realignment of West Coast Highway. Report received from Environmental Protection Authority recommends modified Option H alignment with reduced environmental impacts while maintaining 350 metre radius curve. 14-day appeal period follows release of report. Main Roads Western Australia advises no difficulty with compliance and construction timeframe April to June 1996 unlikely to be compromised.

motions.title: Lake Monger Management Plan
motions.description: Information report on Lake Monger Management Plan completed May 1993 and adopted by former Perth City Council. Plan comprises background and management sections covering lake, fauna, recreational use, access, landscape, maintenance, education/research, signs and reserve zoning. Rehabilitation Plan established eleven zones for priority work. Initial priorities Zones 7-11 from freeway footbridge north to Dodd Street reserve. Budget 1995/96 provision of $70,000 for rehabilitation work and $291,000 for operating/maintenance plus capital works of $55,000.

motions.title: Garden Week at Perry Lakes Reserve
motions.description: Approval for conduct of Garden Week 1996 at Perry Lakes Reserve 18-23 April 1996. Nursery Industries Association proposes establishment of permanent infrastructure including pathways and reticulation. Agreement includes $6,000 fee from Association and Town's promotional support. Proposal for shared cost master plan development estimated $6,000 total with Town's contribution $3,000. Some Member concern expressed but majority supported recommendation.

motions.title: Coastal Management - Beach Protection Investigation
motions.description: Approval to engage Department of Transport to investigate beach protection options for Town coastal strip following erosion damage in early winter 1995. Initial investigative work estimated $21,000. Department of Transport funding may be available on 3:1 basis (3 parts Department, 1 part Town). Study undertaken separately from intended study on beachfront facilities. Cr Smith indicated intention to submit Notice of Motion to next meeting.

motions.title: Cat Sterilisation Scheme
motions.description: Information report on Cat Sterilisation Scheme conducted March to June for past two years. Scheme results in reduction of cat population. Intention to continue scheme. Background includes: approximately 10,000 cats euthanased annually by Cat Welfare Society; unwanted cat population remains high; cats produce three litters per year with 2-9 kittens (mean 4.4); cats prey on native birds, mammals and reptiles. Document appears incomplete (ends mid-page).

motions.title: Cat Sterilisation Subsidy Scheme
motions.description: Proposal to commence a cat sterilisation subsidy scheme in conjunction with the Cat Haven, with an estimated cost of $3,000 to be charged to the Cat Sterilisation Programme budget item.

motions.title: Works Bonds Fees and Charges 1995/96
motions.description: Adoption of the table of works bonds for 1995/96 as proposed, effective from 9 August 1995. The bonds cover residential and commercial developments.

motions.title: Subiaco Oval Events Funding
motions.description: Request from Department of Transport for contribution of $5,000 for promotional campaign to encourage football patrons to utilise public transport when attending Subiaco Oval. Council refused the request.

motions.title: Financial Statements Period Ended 30 April 1995
motions.description: Receiving of financial statements for the period ended 30 April 1995.

motions.title: Accounts for Payment
motions.description: Confirmation of schedule of accounts for payment in accordance with Local Government Accounting Directions 1994.

motions.title: 1995/96 Draft Budget Adoption
motions.description: Formal adoption of the 1995/96 budget for the financial year ending 30 June 1996, including operating, capital, reserve and cash flow budgets. Also establishes general rates, minimum rate, penalty rates, swimming pool inspection fees, and early payment incentive scheme.

motions.title: Significant Accounting Policies Adoption
motions.description: Adoption of Significant Accounting Policies for financial reporting and appointment of Executive Manager Corporate and Customer Services as Principal Accounting Officer.

motions.title: Deed - City of Perth Rate Arrears and Deferred Rates
motions.description: Council to enter into a Deed with the City of Perth regarding arrears and deferred rates levied prior to 1 July 1994, with Mayor and Chief Executive Officer authorised to sign and seal the document.

motions.title: $1 Million Capital Expenditure Reserve
motions.description: Receiving advice from Minister for Local Government on Government decision to provide $1 million for capital expenditure reserve, and transfer of funds to Capital Improvements section of Area Improvement Reserve.

motions.title: Matthews Netball Centre Redevelopment Report
motions.description: Receiving report relating to proposed redevelopment of Matthews Netball Centre, including scope of work, indicative costs and potential funding sources.

motions.title: 1995 Classic Car Rally Event
motions.description: Approval for use of Perry Lakes Drive and Reabold Hill Drive on 10 September 1995 for part of the 1995 Classic Car Rally, subject to various conditions including police and motor sports approvals, parking arrangements, public liability insurance, and a $2,000 bond.

motions.title: Review of Beach Front Facilities
motions.description: Motion to commence preparation of a report on assessment of existing beach front facilities and to invite public comment on future needs and facilities. Amendments clarified the scope to preliminary assessment and defined the geographic area of study.

motions.title: Vary Order of Business
motions.description: Procedural motion to vary the order of business to bring forward urgent business item regarding Ocean Gardens Retirement Estate.

motions.title: Confirmation of Minutes
motions.description: Minutes of the Ordinary Meeting held on 18 December 2007 to be confirmed

motions.title: Pandora Drive - Traffic
motions.description: Options for addressing traffic speed and volume on Pandora Drive. Amendment moved by Cr Berry to prepare traffic treatment plans including design options 2, 8 and 9, lost 1/3. Second amendment by Cr Watson to evaluate traffic treatment options for presentation to Council, carried 3/1. Final amendment by Cr Berry to present preferred option, lost 2/7.

motions.title: Cambridge Street - Kerbside Parking (Northwood to Holyrood)
motions.description: Review of kerbside parking in Cambridge Street from Northwood Street to Holyrood Street following completion of Coles shopping centre in November 2007.

motions.title: Cambridge Street - Kerbside Parking (Holyrood to Town Hall)
motions.description: Review of kerbside parking on northern side of Cambridge Street from Holyrood Street to Leederville Town Hall, requested by adjacent businesses to change from 1 Hour to 2 Hour parking.

motions.title: Holyrood Street - Kerbside Parking
motions.description: Review of kerbside parking in southern section of Holyrood Street, requested by businesses to change from 1 Hour to 2 Hour parking.

motions.title: Railway Parade / Kimberley Street roundabout construction
motions.description: Council considered progressing a 25 metre diameter roundabout at the intersection of Railway Parade and Kimberley Street in West Leederville, including service relocation, land acquisition, and staged construction over two years.

motions.title: Railway Parade / Southport Street roundabout approval
motions.description: Council approved a mini roundabout design at the intersection of Railway Parade and Southport Street in West Leederville with chicanes to manage traffic flow and a Black Spot Grant application.

motions.title: Selby Street / Grantham Street traffic signal upgrade planning
motions.description: Council endorsed the planning work for upgrading traffic signal phasing and geometry at the Selby Street and Grantham Street intersection, including right turn arrows and lane extensions, with community consultation to follow.

motions.title: Road resurfacing five-year program 2008/2009-2012/2013
motions.description: Council approved funding for a five-year road resurfacing program and noted the need for annual review and comprehensive data collection every five years to maintain road network condition.

motions.title: Boulevard median landscape improvement Howtree to Empire Avenue
motions.description: Council approved landscape improvement works including soil replacement, irrigation system upgrade, and new plantings at The Boulevard median, with consideration of public art at Grantham Street intersection.

motions.title: Coastal dunes rabbit control program
motions.description: Council endorsed a regional rabbit control program in coastal dunes between February and April 2008, coordinated with other coastal local governments and funded by Swan Catchment Council.

motions.title: Community Safety and Crime Prevention Plan questionnaire
motions.description: Council endorsed a revised questionnaire to gather community feedback on crime and safety issues for development of the Town's Community Safety and Crime Prevention Plan, with planned endorsement in July 2008.

motions.description: Council noted that no items were dealt with under delegated authority by the Chief Executive Officer during the 2007/2008 Christmas/New Year recess period from 19 December 2007 to 11 February 2008.

Tamala Park Regional Council - Local Structure Plan. Report seeking comment from Council on the Tamala Park Local Structure Plan (LSP) for land parcels bounded by suburbs of Mindarie and Clarkson, Neerabup Road to north, Mitchell Freeway to east, Tamala Park Landfill to south, and coastal foreshore/Indian Ocean to west. LSP developed by project team including TPG Town Planning, Syrinx Environmental, Douglas Partners, TABEC, and multiple other consultants. Principles include lifestyle and housing choice, effective land and infrastructure use, long-term environmental health, identity and inclusiveness, economic health, and community governance. Report details opportunities and constraints including transport/road network, land use, landform, servicing/infrastructure, community facilities, and environmental considerations. Design philosophy addresses residential density near Clarkson Rail Station, solar access, environmental conservation including rare vegetation and green link connectivity to coast and Neerabup National Park, public open space design prioritising surveillance and crime minimisation, activity centres, and employment opportunities.

Wembley Golf Course 2023/24 performance report. Members: 20% increase in membership in 2023. Rounds: 195,000+ rounds delivered in 2023, 65,000+ mini golf rounds, 26,000,000 balls hit on driving range. Golf shop retail sales: $2,000,000+. Customer transactions: 389,000+. Cart hires: 30,000+. Turf maintenance: 720,000m2 irrigated turf with 1,700+ Rain Bird Irrigation sprinklers.

Trackman Range Technology project at Wembley Golf Course. Trackman Range technology unveiled at 80 bay driving range as first facility in WA. Technology allows players to track shots using 21-inch on-site touchscreens or mobile app. System emphasises purposeful practice with actionable data points in real-time. Installation resulted in significant increase in revenue and patronage.

Wembley Golf Course PGA Centre for Learning & Performance project. Upgrades to systems and facilities to latest technology for golf coaching and club fitting completed in June 2024. Official launch planned for later in 2024. Improvements now available to public.

Interactive Walking Trail Maps project. Town upgraded walking trails experience through introduction of new interactive maps. Maps equipped with dynamic zooming, comprehensive trail details, vivid photographs, and real-time mobile tracking. Hosted on Town's website with both digital and printable versions.

Property management report. In addition to 51 leases and licences from previous year (particularly to sporting clubs and restaurants), Town granted consent to sublease to Alchemy Saunas for underutilised space under Clancy's at City Beach and facilitated partial sale of WALGA building at West Leederville. Increase in requests to subleases from tenants. Lake Monger Recreation Club proposal for padel tennis sublease currently being assessed.

South City Beach Kiosk report. Notable structure designed by architect Tony Brand in 1970 with Brutalist and Organic styles. Closed since 2013. Expression of Interest invited March 2024 for future use. Town considering proposals for future use including planning and compliance requirements, costs, and viability. Council anticipated to form final decision on future use in 2024/25 financial year.

Procurement report. Increase in number of goods and services procured through Contracts & Leasing team in 23/24: 28 RFQs, 19 RFTs, and 4 EOIs run. All tenders, RFQs and EOIs conducted in accordance with Purchasing Policy 072 for transparent, equitable, competitive purchasing fully compliant with Local Government Act 1995 and Part 4 of Local Government (Functions and General) Regulations 1996. Improvements to Request for Tender process replacing award letters with formal instrument of agreement.

National Competition Policy compliance report. Town has received no complaints or findings of anti-competitive behaviour or been subject to any legal actions for anti-competitive behaviour, anti-trust, or monopoly practices during 23/24.

Bold Park Aquatic Premieres 'The Pool' partnership. Town of Cambridge partnered with Black Swan State Theatre Company of WA for world premiere of The Pool by Steve Rodgers at Bold Park Aquatic in February 2024, presented in association with Perth Festival. Production transformed Bold Park Aquatic into stage set against bushland. Nearly 8,000 people attended across 15 shows. Production showcased diverse talent and highlighted facility as landmark of cultural and recreational significance.

Department of Fire and Emergency Services Wear Orange Wednesday event. State Emergency Services (SES) Volunteer and Department of Fire & Emergency Services (DFES) crews conducted vertical rescue demonstration using approved area of Quarry Amphitheatre with media present to film on 21 May 2024.

Community Perception Indicators for environment report. Platinum Waterwise Council Status maintained in 2023/24. Urban Forest Strategy goals update commenced in 2023/24 to re-establish goals. Fleet transition in progress for hybrid/electric vehicles anticipated complete by 2024/25. Waste diversion from landfill goal: increase from 57.45%. 2022 benchmark scores: Waste management 58, Efforts for sustainable practices 50, Conservation and environmental management 56, Streetscapes/trees/verges 59, Building and maintaining roads 53. Industry average: 49, 53, 53, 48, 77. Industry high: 68, 68, 64, 67, 68.

Environmental management report for 1.3 Built Environment. Key information on Asset Management, Building Management, Engineering, Sustainability, Waste, and Parks and Natural Environment services. Galup (Lake Monger) Management Plan report. Draft in development following considerable community and traditional owner consultation. Town revised expired Lake Monger Management Plan. Key actions include revegetation of under-utilised turf areas, improved water quality testing program, and renaming of Lake Monger to traditional Noongar name of Galup. Plan will be considered by Council in July 2024.

Strategic Asset Management Plan and related plans report. Strategic Asset Management Plan current, due for review in 2025/26. Infrastructure Asset Management Plans (Portfolio) adopted in 2024. Building Asset Management Plans (Portfolio) adopted in 2024.

Perry Lakes Management Plan and Masterplan 2021-2031 report. Current plan implementation continued in 2023/24. Improved monitoring of water quality and lake levels following Herdsman Main Drain diversion project. Revegetation of lake banks by Friends of Perry Lakes. Installation of fauna attracting structures such as 'Cockitrough' cockatoo drink fountain.

Natural Areas Strategy 2022-2032 report. Strategy continues to guide management of Town's 147ha of bushland, lake systems and dunes. Actions relate to management of invasive species, fauna, water quality, and maintenance.
Sustainability Strategy report. Sustainability Working Group to be established by end of 2024. Interim Strategy to be developed during 2025 in conjunction with community representatives.

Coastal Hazard Risk Management Adaptation Plan (CHRMAP) report. Key actions undertaken include coastal monitoring program in collaboration with other coastal councils and development of Foreshore Management Plan currently in early scope development.
Waste Management Strategy 2020-2025 report. All 10 actions on target to be achieved by end of June 2025.

Urban Forest Strategy 2020-2023 report. Town's first Urban Forest Strategy expired, revised strategy currently in development. New risks to urban forest including significant effect of Polyphagus shot-hole borer on urban canopies around Perth.
Integrated Movement Strategy report. To be developed in 2025/26 incorporating principles and objectives of Bike Plan (now expired) and Walking Trail Strategy (rescinded).

Public open space and natural environment report for 3.1. Total of 43.9% (975ha) of Town's area classified as public open space, including parks like Perry Lakes Reserve and Galup (Lake Monger) managed by Town.

Tree Protection on Private Land report. Scheme Amendment and Policy advertising on hold by DPLH pending outcome of similar proposal by City of Nedlands. Town actively exploring alternative options for tree protection on private land as permission to advertise amendment likely to be rejected.

Tree Compliance Bonds and Associated Fees report. May 2023: Council adopted fees for street tree protection where building works approved. April 2024: Reduced verge street tree preservation bonds and administration fees endorsed. Fees subsequently charged with building applications. January 2024: New tree compliance role filled for proactive intervention. Building sites inspected increased from 39 to 94. 28 compliance issues identified and resolved. In 2023 one developer required to fund removal/replacement for tree death. Up to 30 June 2024, five more developers charged replacement costs.

Galup (Lake Monger) Management Plan development report. Strategic management planning for 10 years. Town began development of Galup (Lake Monger) Management Plan 2024-2034 to direct activities and projects. Community consultation on draft plan and Council endorsement expected from July 2024. Draft plan includes actions for lake edge revegetation, improved water quality monitoring, and implementation of name change to traditional Galup.

Saving Our Snake-Necked Turtle Project report. Town joined forces with Murdoch University and South West Metropolitan Alliance for project. Town's wetlands at Perry Lakes and Galup (Lake Monger) home to populations of snake-necked turtle under threat. Town committed to funding partnership providing community opportunities to support program.

Accelerated Urban Forest Planting Program report. Town delivered accelerated program installing total of 1,600 street and park trees. Additional 1,000 trees planted during 23-24 in response to increased urban density and environmental threats including Polyphagous shot-hole borer. New tree protection measures implemented including trial of tree compliance officer to monitor trees adjacent building sites.

Sustainability and Climate Change report for 3.2. Waste: 79,811 general waste, recycling and garden organics bins collected monthly. 98% green waste diverted from landfill in 23/24. 77% recyclables diverted from landfill. Climate resilience: 1,500 stormwater drainage pits and 106km connecting pipes inspected and cleaned.

Food Organics Green Organics (FOGO) Waste Project report. From 1 July 2024, Town introducing FOGO waste program to reduce waste to landfill. More than 10,000 households (single dwelling residences only) receiving weekly FOGO collection. General waste bins transitioning to fortnightly collections. Project progressed significantly in 2023/24 including development of education and communications program.
E-waste drop off days tonnes report. 2023/24: 23.25, 2022/23: 20.1, 2021/22: 18.1.

Waste composition report showing general waste, recycling, and green waste tonnes. 2023/24: General waste 5,798.40 tonnes, Recycling 2,688.08 tonnes, Green waste 2,956.25 tonnes. 2022/23: General waste 5,831.28, Recycling 2,790.82, Green waste 2,876.50. 2021/22: General waste 5,991.51, Recycling 2,985.53, Green waste 2,946.26.

E-waste drop off days per tonne report showing recycled and repurposed/donated tonnes. 2023/24: Recycled 16.25, Repurposed/Donated 7.5. 2022/23: Recycled 12, Repurposed/Donated 8.1. 2021/22: Recycled 12.6, Repurposed/Donated 5.5.

Town of Cambridge Wins 2024 Stormwater WA Awards for Excellence. Town won award for Excellence in Integrated Stormwater Design for Galup (Lake Monger) Swale Refurbishment project recognising efforts in stormwater management and environmental care. Galup (Lake Monger) Reserve key wildlife habitat and drought refuge on Swan Coastal Plain. Swale maintains water quality through natural filtration. Project aimed to improve stormwater quality by refurbishing nutrient-stripping vegetation and sedimentation basins with landscape architecture services by Josh Byrne & Associates.

Galup (Lake Monger) Swale Refurbishment project details. Project involved removing 500 invasive trees, clearing over 1ha weeds, planting 30,000+ new plants, removing 1,000+ tonnes debris. New conservation fencing installed. Fauna management included relocating 40 turtles and installing features to enhance aquatic habitats.

Beam E-Scooters Now Available in City Beach. Town's 12-month shared e-scooter service trial commenced April 2024 with Beam. Up to 120 purple e-scooters available for hire connecting from Pesholm Dog Beach (City of Stirling) along coast to City Beach.

Green Fleet Transition - Light vehicle fleet replacement program. Program allows Town's corporate vehicles replacement with more energy efficient vehicles. Town replaced 13 commuter vehicles with hybrid models and 7 fuel efficient utility vehicles delivered. Charging points installed at Works Depot and Administration Centre powered by renewable sources. Procurement process underway to replace all pool and Ranger parking vehicles with full electric vehicles during 2024/2025. RFT for electric vehicle closed and report to award contract to be brought to Council in October 2025.

Works - drainage management report. Maintenance and inspections performed on 5,862 drainage pits and 106 km connecting pipes as needed. As part of proactive drainage education program, 1,500 stormwater drainage pits inspected and cleaned. 20 high-priority drainage defects in City Beach repaired to improve performance and extend asset life.

Bushfire management and control report. To mitigate bushfire risk, owners of private residential and vacant land within Town subject to requirements of Town's Firebreak Notice between 1 November to 31 March. Rangers conduct inspections to assess and enforce compliance. Wembley Golf Course updated bushfire risk management strategy in November 2023 as part of annual review prior to summer season.

Emergency management report. Town continues to partner with adjoining local governments in Local Emergency Management Committee (LEMC) to review and develop preparedness to respond to and recover from emergencies.

Built Environment infrastructure and building asset values report. Total value of managed assets: $435 million. Drainage: 5,892 pits and 104 km pipes. Carparks managed: 84. Buildings managed: 102. Parks infrastructure items: 10,222.

Town building structural audits and asbestos management report. All Town buildings assessed and if necessary listed on asbestos register. Removal and mitigation of high-risk sites undertaken. Town continues monitoring with annual building asbestos register update. Structural audits also undertaken annually to capture structural concerns. Due to large building volume and limited funding, approximately 7 buildings audited annually.

Compliance Services report. Compliance Services ensures building and development carried out in accordance with permits and approvals and construction sites maintained to avoid adverse community impact. Responsible for Town's private swimming pool barrier inspection program. 2023/24 data: 69 development matters investigated (unauthorised development or contrary to approval), 47 building compliance matters (unauthorised work, land affected, property damage, unsafe structures), 213 private property matters (stormwater, sand drift, materials storage, unsightly land, boundary fences, trees).

Prosecution proceedings and fine report. Town instigated prosecution regarding unauthorised retaining wall and front fence at private property in City Beach. Fine of $7,500 imposed. Owner required to pay Town's costs of $2,316.

Verges and Verge Permits report. 180 verge compliance investigations conducted (unsafe verges, unauthorised storage, non-compliance with hard landscaping and vegetation policies). 87 verge permits issued.
Construction sites investigations report. 168 sites investigated for range of issues (material storage, dust, rubbish, noise and other nuisance and safety concerns).
Private swimming pool inspections report. 557 private swimming pool barriers inspected for compliance with Building Regulations 2012 including multiple site visits to ensure compliance achieved.

Public Building Inspections report. In 2023/2024, 35 public buildings inspected for compliance with Health (Public Buildings) Regulations 1992. Particular attention paid to emergency exits, locks, signage, evacuation plans, fire prevention/control, and documentation. All non-compliance subject to follow-up inspections.

Effluent Disposal Systems/Sewer In-fill report. Areas of City Beach unable to connect to sewer requiring onsite wastewater disposal. Two applications for new Aerobic Treatment Units (ATUs) and one septic tank approved. Six decommissioning applications received.

Building Services report. Building Approvals: $233,596.15 total fees generated. 87 swimming pool construction applications. 335 Certified Building Permits ($142,191,162 estimated value). 65 Uncertified Building Permits ($1,880,135 estimated value). 12 Building Approval Certificates ($97,550 estimated value). 41 Full/Partial Demolition Permits ($1,221,540 estimated value). 15 Occupancy Permits ($339,224 estimated value). 468 total applications received ($145,729,611 total estimated value).

Local Planning Policy 3.1: Residential Built Form (Streetscape) report. Adopted March 2024 with modifications relating to crossovers provisions and update to modern practices. Policy referred to WAPC for final approval in 2024/25.

Movement and Access infrastructure report for 3.4. Dedicated Traffic and Transport team established within Engineering Services for better resource and technical capacity. 2023/24 major projects completed: Grantham Street Multi-Intersection, Ruislip Safe Active Street, Lake Monger Drive Southwest Car Park, upgrade and greening of five laneways, rehabilitation of three Cambridge Street sections in urban corridor under nighttime conditions.

$1.4m Project Drives Road Safety Improvements. Town recently completed 2023-24 road resurfacing project. Managing 190km sealed roads and lanes, project prioritised areas based on surface age and condition. Significant works from Berkeley Crescent, Caithness and Hornsey Roads, Linden Gardens, Orrel, and Kirkdale Avenues in Floreat to St Leonards Avenue in West Leederville delivering smoother, quieter, safer pavements and extended road lifespan.

Roads, footpaths and traffic management report. 194 km roads managed. 218 km footpaths managed. 77 bus shelters. 85 Traffic Management Planning applications assessed. 83 Vehicle crossover applications assessed.
Car Park Management report. 82 car parks maintained and inspected in 2023/24 including pothole repairs and renewal of kerbs and footpaths. Up to 8 programmed street sweeping operations per year.

Right of Way Management report. 21.5km right-of-ways maintained and inspected in 2023/24 including three scheduled cleaning operations per right-of-way (illegal waste removal, weed control, tree pruning, street sweeping).

Road and Path Network Management report. 172km sealed roads maintained and inspected in 2023/24 (street sweeping, pothole repairs, kerb renewal). 217km footpaths maintained and inspected (kerb and footpath renewal). 89 bus shelters maintained and inspected.

Signalised Intersections and Mid-Block Crossings assessment report. Five intersections/crossings assessed for potential upgrades: Railway Parade pedestrian signalized crossing, Lake Monger Drive pedestrian signalized crossing, Three intersections on Harborne Street (Grantham St, Ruislip St, Cambridge St), Salvado Road and Jersey Street.

Transportation Project Reviews report. Four reviews underway: Cambridge Street Traffic Study Blackspot Project Review, Grantham Street Multi-Intersection Treatment Review and Evaluation, Wembley Speed Zoning Review, Ruislip Street Safe Active Street (SAS) Review and Evaluation.

Traffic signal upgrade: Harborne & Cambridge Street Intersection. Project aims to enhance efficiency and safety by introducing right-turn arrow to regulate right turns, reducing risk of right-angle and right-turn crashes. Requires extensive upgrades to aging MRWA signal infrastructure. Town working in partnership with MRWA for cost-effective approach.

Intersection improvement (design phase): Jon Sanders Drive – Powis Street (Harborne Street). Aims to enhance pedestrian safety and alleviate traffic congestion. Total project estimated at $3 million with two-thirds funded by MRRG Improvement Program. Remaining cost shared equally between Town of Cambridge and City of Stirling. Year 1 design completed. Year 2 design scheduled 2024/2025. Construction planned 2026/2027 pending approvals/funding.

Pedestrian safety improvement: Selby & Cambridge Street Signals. Traffic signal phasing upgrade aims to enhance pedestrian safety. Multi-year phased project due to design complexities and MRWA approval timelines. Year 1 design commenced 2022/2023. Stage 2 Traffic Signal approvals granted 2023/2024. Detailed design planned 2024/2025. Construction proposed 2025/2026 pending approvals/funding.

Ruislip St Safe Active Street corrective actions report. Design and construction of traffic calming measures along 4.4km route to lower speeds. On-road cycling and active transport facility providing east-west route through Town, connecting Leederville Train Station to coast via Boulevard shared path. Fully funded by Department of Transport grant. Includes traffic reduction/calming measures aiming for <1,500 vehicles/day and 30 km/h speeds. Completed 2023/2024 with performance review scheduled 2024/2025.

District distributor road rehabilitation and asset renewal report. Successfully completed pavement rehabilitation and road resurfacing on five district distributor road sections to preserve condition, prevent deterioration and eliminate hazards. Two-thirds funded by Metropolitan Regional Road Group.

Our Town governance and performance report for section 4. Community Perception Indicators benchmark showing 2022 scores: Governing organisation 45, Value for money from rates 46, Council's leadership 30, Community consultation 28, Clear vision communication 19, Understanding community needs 18, Listens to residents 15, Explains decisions 13. Industry average: 53, 43, 47, 43, 30, 30, 28, 24. Industry high: 67, 62, 60, 60, 50, 58, 53, 39.

Strategies and Informing Plans for governance. Strategic Workforce Plan to be adopted July 2024. Communications Strategy adopted April 2024. Customer Experience Plan and Charter in development to be finalised November 2024. Community Engagement Framework adopted February 2024. Information and Communications Technology Strategy current. Project Management Framework to be reviewed to include new TechnologyOne system.

Activity Base Costing (ABC) Review report. Review to more efficiently allocate expenses across organisation completed in 2023/24. Implementation planned 2024/25 to improve financial reporting and transparency.

Town of Cambridge Recordkeeping Plan report. Town complies with State Records Act 2000. Recordkeeping Plan approved by State Records Commission 7 June 2024, due for review 2029. Amended Organisational Recordkeeping Policy approved by Council 23 April 2024. ECM recordkeeping system complies with State Records retention/disposal requirements. All employees complete Recordkeeping, ECM, and Privacy training during induction.

Freedom of Information Statement report. FOI Act requires Information Commissioner to report to WA Parliament on FOI Act operation annually. Town of Cambridge FOI Statistical Return 2023-24 submitted to Office of Information Commissioner 8 July 2024. Town reviewed and published Information Statement submitted 22 May 2024 per FOI Act, available on Town website.

Records Training report. Information Management team committed to training all current and new employees in recordkeeping requirements and Town's recordkeeping system use. Leading inter-departmental collaboration to address technological changes. 26 valid Freedom of Information applications received and finalised in 2023/24. More than 100 staff trained in recordkeeping. More than 360 archive boxes reviewed and processed.

Privacy and Data management report. Information Technology and Management team introduced two new management practices for governance. Published Privacy Policy and Data Breach Policy. State legislation on Privacy and Responsible Information Sharing (PRIS) due 2024. Proactive plan established with key tasks and milestones for implementation. Final review and implementation upon legislation release.

Strategic Workforce Plan report. Staff Retention and Attraction Strategy adopted by Council April 2024 to attract and retain talent. Learning and Development Strategy centralising training through People & Culture. Implementation scheduled 2024/25. Gap Analysis to identify succession planning and critical skills improvements. Pilot commenced May 2024 with full rollout 2024/25.

Health, Safety and Wellness report. Town completed Three Steps to Safety Audit (WHS) November 2023 by LGIS. Proactive interventions provided including skin checks, health screenings, audiometric testing. People@Work Consultative Committee established with employee representatives to develop employee wellness initiatives and manage psychosocial safety risk.

LGPro Local Government Management Challenge 2024 report. Cambridge registered two teams of emerging leaders in 2024 professional development challenge. National contest running 25 years, first time Town participated. 12 nominated employees evaluated on energy, chemistry, effectiveness, creative thinking at HBF Park May. Teams supported and mentored by two managers. Both teams performed well with positive feedback.
Internal Audit Plan report. Development of three-year plan for efficient and effective internal audit processes in 2023/24. Nine completed internal audits in 2023/24. Two internal audits in progress.

ICT Services report. All ICT staff ITIL4 certified ensuring high-level service implementation. All Helpdesk queries handled by new ICT Service Management system providing quality reporting, streamlined communications, appropriate audit trail. 93.84% Helpdesk ticket resolution compliance (Target 90%). 7hr 56min average Priority 1 Incident resolution (Target 8 hours). Cyber Incident Response Plan used for all cyber security incidents.

Wembley Golf Course IT Centralisation report. Wembley Golf Course now centralised with Town's IT infrastructure, creating consistent end user support and standardised cyber security approach for managing Town's ICT systems.

Digital Transformation and ICT Strategy (Year 3 of 5) report. Five-year Digital Transformation and ICT Strategy on track. Completed projects include backup infrastructure resilience audit and remediation, Wembley Golf Course IT centralisation, IT Equipment upgrade, Finance and Leave dashboards, OAG 2021 audit findings, Library public access computer upgrade, centrally managed email signatures, CiAnywhere Supply Chain Management, CiAnywhere Enterprise Asset Management, Intramaps improvements, IT Service Desk Management System, Business Continuity framework, Cyber Security Incident Response Plan and Testing.

TechnologyOne SaaS – Upgrade: Enterprise Asset Management. The CiAnywhere upgrade rollout continued with release of the Enterprise Asset Management module, consolidating multiple asset registers into a single source of truth, introducing work orders, scheduled maintenance records, and project management.

ICT Business Continuity Plans. The ICT Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plans have been successfully implemented with ongoing review and maintenance. Mobile Device Management System has been introduced to improve efficiency and security.

Cyber Security: Essential Eight. ICT security has been significantly enhanced with various measures to strengthen the Town's security posture. A new cyber security training platform was launched and the Cyber Security Incident Response Plan has been completed and put into practice in August 2023.

Customer Experience Plan and Charter. A Customer Experience Plan was developed in 2023/24 to streamline and improve customer experience. A review and update of the Town's Customer Service Charter to assess current service level commitments is underway, intended to be completed by the end of 2024.

Governance Process Improvement. New process and software solutions were implemented in January and February 2024, including a Compliance Calendar, Resolution Register, and Recording Exercise of Delegations. An external consultant completed a review of Regulation 5 and Regulation 17 audits, with draft report identifying 78 business improvements.

Doc Assembler Minutes and Agenda Software. Implementation of new minutes and agenda software in August 2023 has significantly improved the accuracy and efficiency of the Town's production of agendas and minutes.

Landline Phone System Replacement. The Town will replace existing out-of-life and out-of-support phone system across the whole Town with soft phone calling capability in 2024/25, providing advanced reporting capabilities and better Customer Services administration.

Own Source Revenue. Key information on financial sustainability through commercial revenue opportunities. Total operating revenue for 2023/24 was $66,311,502 with 12,210 rateable properties. Rates revenue was $27,118,914.

Quarry Amphitheatre Strategic Business Plan. A long-term strategic plan was adopted by Council in June 2024. The Strategic Business Plan incorporates a marketing and business development plan and will inform budget development over the next five years.

The Boulevard Centre Marketing Plan. Past hirers were contacted for feedback on venue and services to inform the development of a marketing plan for the Boulevard Centre, with a view to driving increased usage.

Bold Park Aquatic. The facility had 413 active members in 2023/24, an increase of 11%. Retail sales of swimwear and accessories were $220,000+, café sales were $230,000, lane and room hire totalled 7,000 hours, and 118 children's birthday parties were hosted between October 2023 and March 2024. A cloud-based booking system roll-out is on track for October 2024.

Parking Revenue and Paid Parking System Upgrades. The Town continued to roll out upgrades to paid parking systems in 2023/24, with cashless parking machines providing greater efficiency and improved data to inform future decisions on parking fees, charges, and restrictions.

Capital Grants, Subsidies and Contributions. The Town receives grant funding from State and Federal programs for capital works projects and contributions from developers as cash-in-lieu of development provisions. Section 19BE of the Local Government (Administration) Regulations 1996 requires disclosure of capital grants, subsidies, and contributions received for renewal or replacement of assets for the past three financial years.

Local Identity - Website and Digital Engagement. The Town website received 763,918 active views and had 207,408 active users during 2023/24. Social media followers increased: Facebook 12,231 followers (11.9% increase), Instagram 2,730 followers (12.1% increase), LinkedIn 1,771 followers (35.9% increase).
Cambridge Library Engagement. Library received 1,653 e-newsletter subscribers, 1,243 Facebook followers and 511 Instagram followers, and 71,428 visits to the library website.

Newsletter Subscribers. Cambridge News had 9,686 subscribers with 24 editions published in 2023/24. Library Reader had 1,563 subscribers with 12 editions. Pool News had 6,484 subscribers with 12 editions. Seniors News had 338 subscribers with 12 editions. Wembley Golf Course e-newsletter had 59,000 subscribers with 14 editions.

Strategic Community Plan. The Town prepared a new Strategic Community Plan 2023-2033, which was adopted by Council on 22 August 2023. The plan was developed based on engagement with more than 1,200 people and identifies four strategic outcomes: Our People, Our Economy, Our Environment, and Our Town.

Corporate Business Plan. Following the adoption of the new Strategic Community Plan 2023-2033 in August 2023, work commenced on updating the Town's Corporate Business Plan 2023/24 to 2026/27. The Corporate Business Plan was adopted by Council in March 2024.

Quarterly and Annual Reporting. Following the Corporate Business Plan's adoption, a quarterly reporting program was implemented to assess and report on the Town's progress towards its strategic objectives. The first quarterly report for 2023/24 was provided to Council in April 2024 and the final quarterly report in July 2024. An annual review of the Corporate Business Plan was conducted as part of the annual budget process.

Communications Strategy. An updated Communications Strategy and Brand Style Guide were adopted by Council in April 2024. The strategy provides guidance to the Town in taking a strategic approach to all Town marketing and communications activities.

Community Engagement Framework. The Town's Community Engagement Framework was updated and adopted by Council in February 2024. The new framework guides and supports Elected Members and the Town's Administration when undertaking engagement activities. Implementation of the framework and associated tools is ongoing and will be further developed in 2024/25.

Floreat Visioning Workshops and Community Working Group. The Town hosted four Floreat Activity Centre Visioning workshops in 2024, which were attended by 254 people. In April 2024, Council resolved to endorse the formation of a Floreat Forum Community Working Group to help guide the Precinct Structure Plan. On 7 May 2024, Council resolved to appoint Elected Members and residents to the group.

Comprehensive Financial Report and Auditor's Report. The Auditor General's independent audit report on the Town of Cambridge's financial report for the year ended 30 June 2024 states that the financial report is based on proper accounts and records, presents fairly the results of operations and financial position, and is in accordance with the Local Government Act 1995.

Padel Monger Proposal - Community Consultation. Report detailing community consultation results on the proposed sublease to Padel Monger Pty Ltd for a portion of Lake Monger Recreation Club's leased premises. Community consultation undertaken with 284 households via letter drop, online survey, social media, and drop-in sessions. Technical reports on acoustics and lighting confirmed compliance with relevant regulations and standards.

Report includes noise conditions, community consultation findings (341 submissions analysed), and policy/statutory implications. Operating hours proposed 7.00am to 9.30pm Monday to Sunday including public holidays. Eight noise management conditions recommended.

Draft Cambridge Library Strategic Plan 2025-2029 report prepared by Sally De Freitas and Teagan Nyeboer, authorised by Luke Gibson, Director Planning and Community Services. The report presents a strategic plan anchored by three pillars (Connection, Collection, and Community) with three associated key themes (community connection, learning and discovery, and operational effectiveness). The plan is informed by a 2024 community survey showing 95% satisfaction rate among 600+ respondents, an internal benchmarking report, and alignment with the WA Public Library Strategy 2022-2026.

Cambridge Library Strategic Plan 2025-2029. West Leederville Precinct Structure Plan assessment report addressing proposed modifications to heights, density codes, laneways, plazas, setbacks, traffic and access, and preparation for readvertising. Report includes planning assessment of precincts 1-4, height and density controls, laneway network analysis, and recommendations for modifications to the structure plan.

Schedule of Modifications document detailing 26 recommended modifications to the West Leederville Precinct Structure Plan Version 1, addressing alignment with regulations, document formatting, height and density controls, plot ratio provisions, laneway and plaza design, setbacks, and transport impact assessment updates.

Plot ratio study for West Leederville Precinct Structure Plan prepared by mackay urbandesign in May 2024. Study models three sites (12-storey and 18-storey developments) to determine appropriate plot ratio controls corresponding to proposed height increases from 9 storeys to 12 and 18 storeys. Findings recommend plot ratio of 4 for 12-storey areas and plot ratio of 6 for 18-storey areas.

Laneway Status and Yields analysis for proposed new laneways and laneway widenings in West Leederville Precinct Structure Plan. Document analyzes 20 laneway locations against Landgate information, measures land take per lot, and assesses how laneway requirements affect floor space allowances. Provides infrastructure contribution analysis showing additional height and plot ratio concessions for properties required to cede land for laneways and plazas.

WLACP Capacity and Yield Analysis - Summary Report prepared by JR, dated 16/07/2024. Document provides dwelling yield estimates and non-residential floorspace estimates for West Leederville Activity Centre Precinct across four precincts (Cambridge High Street, Kerr Street to Abbotsford Street, Southport Street, and Leederville Link) under moderate and strong growth scenarios.

West Leederville Precinct Structure Plan - Transport Impact Assessment prepared by Stantec Australia Pty Ltd for the Town of Cambridge. Report dated 30 September 2024 (Revision 003). Document provides analysis of traffic operations, transport networks, parking supply, and recommendations for transport integration across the West Leederville Activity Centre including Cambridge Street, Southport Street, Railway Parade, and proposed laneway networks.

West Leederville Precinct Structure Plan - Strategic Direction, Existing Situation, Proposed Changes to Transport Networks, Integration with Surrounding Area, and Analysis of Transport Network. Comprehensive planning document covering parking requirements, freight and deliveries, existing land uses, road networks, traffic volumes, pedestrian/cycle networks, public transport services, parking supply, crash data analysis, proposed laneway networks, road hierarchy changes, pedestrian and cycling infrastructure proposals, public transport improvements, and traffic impact assessment for future development scenarios.

West Leederville Precinct Structure Plan - Analysis of Transport Network. Detailed technical analysis of intersection performance using SIDRA software across multiple scenarios (2024 existing traffic, 2036 background traffic without development, 2036 background traffic with development, and mitigation measures). Includes analysis of six key intersections: Cambridge Street/Kimberley Street, Cambridge Street/Southport Street, Cambridge Street/Loftus Street, Railway Parade/Kimberley Street, Railway Parade/Southport Street, and Railway Parade/Loftus Street. Also includes parking supply analysis and street design recommendations for Cambridge Street, Southport Street, Northwood Street, and Railway Parade.

West Leederville Precinct Structure Plan - Review of Proposed Street Designs. Transport Impact Assessment report containing analysis of Northwood Street street design options (Option 1: Footpath Widening, Angled Parking, and On-street Cycling; Option 2: One side Parallel Parking and Separated Bike Lanes), Railway Parade improvements, and SIDRA traffic modelling results for key intersections (Cambridge Street/Kimberley Street, Cambridge Street/Southport Street, Cambridge Street/Loftus Street, Railway Parade/Kimberley Street, Railway Parade/Southport Street, Railway Parade/Loftus Street/Thomas Street/Railway Street).

SIDRA intersection traffic modelling analysis for West Leederville Precinct Plan. Contains movement summaries and Level of Service (LOS) performance data for multiple intersections including Railway Pde/Loftus St/Thomas St/Railway St, Cambridge St/Kimberley St, Cambridge St/Southport St, Cambridge St/Loftus St, Railway Pde/Kimberley St (roundabout), and Railway Pde/Southport St (roundabout), analysed for AM, PM, and Saturday scenarios with and without development.

SIDRA Intersection traffic modelling analysis for West Leederville Precinct Plan development scenarios. Includes movement summaries and performance analysis for multiple intersection sites (Cambridge St/Southport St, Cambridge St/Loftus St, Railway Pde/Kimberley St, Railway Pde/Southport St, Railway Pde/Loftus St/Thomas St/Railway St, Cambridge St/Kimberley St) under various time periods (AM, PM, SAT) and mitigation scenarios.

West Leederville Precinct Structure Plan - technical appendix containing SIDRA intersection traffic analysis reports for multiple sites (Cambridge St/Loftus St, Railway Pde/Kimberley St, Railway Pde/Southport St, Railway Pde/Loftus St/Thomas St/Railway St) under development scenarios (AM, PM, SAT peak periods) and structure plan implementation documentation

West Leederville Precinct Structure Plan (WLPSP) Explanatory Report - Part 2 covering Centre Context, Movement, and Activity sections including laneways requirements, existing and proposed land uses, employment, retail needs assessment, and transport network planning.

West Leederville Precinct Structure Plan report detailing sections on residential dwelling targets, urban form, heritage, laneways, plazas, resource conservation and implementation actions. Schedule of 39 community submissions received during public consultation for DA23/0247, all objecting to the proposed betting agency use. Submissions numbered 1-39 addressing concerns about gambling harm, impact on children, family-friendly atmosphere, extended operating hours, antisocial behaviour, noise, parking, and character of suburb.

Schedule of community submissions regarding planning application DA23/0247 for change of use (additional use for betting agency) at 5 Howtree Place, Floreat (The Sporting Globe). Contains 38 numbered submissions from local residents and stakeholders.

Planning application DA23/0247 for proposed change of use from 'Tavern' to 'Tavern' and 'Betting Agency (Use Not Listed) (Incidental Use)' at Lot 100 (No. 94/5) Howtree Place, Floreat. Officer report with administration recommendation to approve, subject to conditions including restriction to two betting terminals only and operating hours of Friday-Saturday 10am-12 midnight, Sunday-Thursday 10am-10pm. Community consultation period received 39 objections, all opposing the proposal.

Schedule of Submissions for planning application DA23/0247. Twenty-one detailed community submissions received, all objecting to the proposed betting terminals at the Sporting Globe. Key concerns raised include: increased gambling harm and addiction risk (particularly harmful impact on vulnerable populations and families), normalization of gambling for young people in proximity to primary school, adverse amenity impacts (noise, anti-social behaviour, traffic, parking), character and safety concerns for family-friendly suburb, early opening hours (6am) promoting early-morning drinking and gambling, proximity to Floreat Park Primary School and children's playground creating inappropriate exposure for minors, duplication with existing TAB facility already in Floreat Forum, combination of alcohol and gambling promoting harmful behaviours, and broader social impacts including family violence, financial distress, and community wellbeing decline.

Restoration of Whadjuk Noongar name Galup to Lake Monger Reserve, officially announced 17 June 2025. Name means 'where the home fires burn' and holds deep cultural significance. Local Planning Policy 3.25: Tree Retention adopted in December 2024. The Policy addresses declining tree canopy within the Town by requiring development approval prior to removing or damaging a 'regulated tree' on private, residential property. A 'regulated tree' is a living tree which has a height of 8m or more, a canopy at least 6m wide and a total trunk circumference of 1m or more that is 1.4m above ground level.

Amendments to Local Planning Policy 3.24: Determining Natural Ground Level. The amendments respond to changes to the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015 and a recent State Administrative Tribunal decision relating to the interpretation of 'natural ground level'. An Elected Member Forum was held on 13 September 2022 to discuss the recommended amendments.

Local Planning Policy 3.24: Determining Natural Ground Levels - Report and proposed amendments following Prosser v Town of Cottesloe tribunal decision. The amendments align the policy with the Deemed Provisions definition of natural ground level and provide guidance for determining NGL where no previous development approval exists. Requires shift from reliance on 1975 Department of Lands & Surveys maps to current site surveys.

Local Planning Policy 3.3: Building Height - Report and proposed amendments to address concerns about increased building height and bulk in residential areas following 2021 R-Codes amendments. Proposes reintroduction of reduced building height for City Beach Precinct (maximum wall height 6.5m, maximum total building heights 7.5m for gable/skillion/concealed roof, 9.0m for hipped/pitched roof) and strengthened design principles regarding topography and streetscape character.

Australia Day Local Government Awards Program 1997 - Report advising that Council has been invited to participate in the Local Government Citizen Awards administered by the National Australia Day Council. The categories of the awards include Australia Day Citizen Award, Australia Day Young Citizen Award, and Australia Day Community Event of the Year Award. Council's involvement would include promotion of the award categories within the community, selection of successful applicants, and presentation of awards, with minimal cost involved.

Report on review of Wembley Golf Complex irrigation system. Current system is 30 years old and requires complete replacement due to age, iron content in bore water, and high operational costs ($125,000 per annum). Specialist consultants Hydro-Plan conducted assessment. Proposed staged replacement program with estimated total cost of $2,766,085. Report details problems with current system including iron build-up causing blockages, uneven water distribution, six separate irrigation zones, and lack of central control. Proposed new system includes two storage lakes (16.5 million litres capacity), pump station, central computer control, weather station, and modern sprinkler design allowing individual control. Construction staged to minimize disruption to golf play. Report notes financial modeling shows cost to maintain existing system for 10 years is estimated at $2,723,000.

Lot 1203 (No. 63) Pearson Street (corner Cromarty Road), Floreat – Proposed change of use: residential to child day care centre (Jellybeans Child Care). Application DA REFERENCE: 61DA - 2006. Site area 1151m2, proposed to accommodate 55 children. Variations sought to Town Planning Scheme No. 1 policy requirements. [private individual — name withheld] [private individual — name withheld] Zoning: Urban; TPS No.1: Residential R12.5. Policy 3.5 allows maximum 25 children (or 40 if site abuts non-residential land), but application proposes 55 children and site abuts residential land uses. Town of Cambridge Residential Design Guidelines require minimum 7.0 metre setback to portico on primary street (Pearson Street) and 4.5 metres on secondary street (Cromarty Road); proposal shows 4.9 metres and 3.0 metres respectively. Fencing requirements: solid wall maximum 0.75 metres with infill open to solid ratio 1:1; proposal shows 0.86 metres with picket fence ratio less than 1:1. Proposed single storey building clad in mix of face and rendered brickwork with colorbond roof. Public notification period (21 days) resulted in two letters of support and seven letters of objection. Support letters cite chronic shortage of childcare places in inner western suburbs following potential closure of ECU Childcare Centre at the end of 2007. Objections cite traffic congestion concerns at busy Pearson Street/Cromarty Road intersection, noise impacts on nearby residential properties, safety concerns for children, and precedent concerns for future commercial zoning changes.

Western Metropolitan Regional Council request for annual contribution. The WMRC sought $50,000 per annum from the Town towards resource recovery services including receipt of household hazardous waste, e-waste, general household waste, mattresses and other recyclables. The proposal included a staged approach with 50% payable in 2019-20, 75% in 2020-21, and 100% in 2021-22.

Donate Life 'Life Sculpture' public art final design and location at City Beach foreshore. Subi East Draft Master Plan - submission. DevelopmentWA released the Subi East draft Master Plan for public comment in July 2020. It is a high-level strategic planning document intended to guide the redevelopment of the former Subiaco Oval and Princess Margaret Hospital, along with the land between Thomas Street, Roberts Road, Haydn Bunton Drive and the Fremantle Railway. Council is recommended to make a submission on the draft Master Plan given proximity and proposed integration with the Town's Medical Precinct and the West Leederville Activity Centre.

Detailed officer report on the Subi East Draft Master Plan released by DevelopmentWA addressing four neighbourhoods (Subi Oval, PMH, Railway, and Mueller Park), minimum 2,700 dwellings, land use objectives, building heights, public open space (9 hectares), pedestrian and cycle networks, and transport movement including traffic impacts on surrounding areas. Report includes detailed analysis of parking provision (3,685 off-street bays and 350 on-street spaces), retail/commercial floorspace, and coordination with West Leederville Activity Centre planning.

Detailed officer report on the Western Australian Planning Commission's interim review of Residential Design Codes Volume 1. Covers proposed modifications to primary street setbacks, lot boundary setbacks, open space requirements, outdoor living areas, building height, landscaping, visual privacy setbacks, solar access/overshadowing, and ancillary dwellings. Report provides analysis of each proposed change with Town's position (supported, not supported, or recommendations for further clarification).

Officer report on the resolution to prepare Local Planning Scheme No. 2. Details the project plan for review of the current Scheme (first gazetted 1998, amended 39 times) and preparation of new scheme. Project plan divided into eight parts: concurrent projects, scheme review, drafting new scheme, initial endorsement, local policy review, public consultation, council approval, and final approval. Proposes delegation of authority to Development Committee to endorse 'guiding principles' for each focus area during preparation process.

Community Sporting and Recreation Facilities Fund (CSRFF) Forward Planning Grant Application for replacement of Sports Amenity Building at Alderbury Sports Ground. The Administration proposes to submit application seeking $435,600 (ex GST) to the Department of Local Government, Sport and Cultural Industries. Application must be submitted by 11 September 2020. Current facility installed approximately 1975 has surpassed useful life and presents issues with disability access, antisocial behaviour and facility standards. Community consultation revealed 80% of respondents considered the design suitable for Alderbury Sports Ground. New facility will include change rooms, kitchen and storage facilities available for hire to sporting clubs and community groups, with sustainability considerations and compliance with all current Australian Standards.

Background describes council report from 8 August 1995 on proposed financial year 1995/96 work including maintenance, capital works, and development (first of multi-stage project with Lake Monger Management Plan funding of $70,000). Key element was negotiation with Aboriginal groups. Details consultation with Bilbulman, Balluruk and Noongar groups at August 1995 site meeting with attendance payment agreed but not requested. Report discusses November 1995 meeting request issue, correspondence with Robert Bropho of Nyungah Circle of Elders, and Aboriginal Affairs Department responses. Outlines four options: unlimited meeting process, limited payment ($5,000 maximum), payment-free process, or project progress without consultation. Recommends Option Two (limited payment) for demonstrating negotiated outcome and likely conclusion.

Report on Town of Cambridge Logo Design Competition. Background describes January 1996 council resolution establishing Logo Selection Panel comprising Mayor, Deputy Mayor, Crs Berry and MacRae, CEO and Executive Manager Corporate and Customer Services, with authorization for consultant advice. Reports 240 design entries received from 165 individuals by 22 December 1995 closing date, two competition categories (Open and Primary School), prize donations (personal computer by Headlam Computers, portable CD player by Floreat Rotary Club). Panel met three times with graphic design assistance from Paul Butcher (Jung Lautrec & Shaw) and Community Development Officer Linda Brnjich. Recommended entry from Open Division was modified to enhance contemporary design with classical type font. Recommendation to keep winning entries and recommended design confidential until official announcement at Town's new Administration/Civic Centre opening.

Comprehensive report on Additional Staff Resources submitted by CEO responding to Deputy Mayor Cr D Berry's request. Report addresses work backlogs and complex issues inherited from restructured City of Perth, proposes temporary or contract personnel to clear backlog prior to 1996/97 financial year. Details projects across four functional areas: Technical Services ($34,000 for asset management, tree management, project estimating system, procedures manual), Development and Environmental Services ($90,000 for records retrieval, procedures review, LARP implementation, streetscape improvements, temporary staff), CEO ($45,000 for strategic planning, performance management, delegation review), and Corporate and Customer Services ($47,100 for clerical assistance, IT support, property consultant, community development officer, library cataloguing). Lists additional tasks potentially completable in three-month establishment phase including finalizing accounts, AGM preparation, budget development, new Local Government Act compliance, insurance broker appointment, computer module implementation, and lease negotiations. Identifies further capital projects recommended for 1996/97 budget inclusion: Coastal Study ($50,000), Recreational Study ($30,000), Bikeplan ($25,000), Right-of-Way Study ($20,000), Residential Design Guidelines ($25,000), and Public Open Space Study ($10,000). Total temporary resource requirement: $216,100; additional projects total: $160,000.

Bold Park Community School – Request for School Site. Report on investigations and discussions with the Bold Park Parents Advisory Council regarding identification of a permanent site for the school. Identification and assessment of seven potential sites; preferred site is The Boulevard Quarry Site (approximately 23,000 m²). Concept design proposes staged development with 30 transportable units over 4 years (2003-2006) with total development cost of $4,675,000. Constraints identified include geotechnical and contamination site assessment, environmental management, Bold Park Aquatic Centre overflow parking requirements, MRS amendment to urban zoning, and proximity to proposed residential subdivision. Financial analysis provided with projected enrolments growing from 219 students in 2003 to 527 in 2007 and operating revenue from $893,000 to $3.7 million. Capital funding proposed from Commonwealth grants ($1,175,000), State low-interest loans ($2,100,000), bank loans ($1,250,000), private loan for community hall ($350,000), and building fund/fundraising ($790,000).

Underground Power Program - Results from a Survey of Property Owners. Survey of 4,360 properties in Floreat, Wembley and West Leederville regarding propensity to pay for underground power installation. 1,846 responses received (42%). Overall 45% indicated willingness to pay (19.1% of total population). Single residential property owners showed 51% support (24% of population). Strata titled units showed only 31.5% support (11.3% of population). No particular geographic concentration of support identified. Previous underground power projects under State Underground Power Program had higher support levels (68-77%).

Community consultation results and final adoption of the Natural Area Strategy 2022-2032. Survey conducted 21 October to 18 November 2022 with 27 responses. Key feedback addressed updates to strategy regarding tree protection, cat control, fire management, and weed control alternatives.

Stakeholder consultation results for Cowden Park renewal. Survey included responses from West Leederville Primary School students, administration, and P&C. Key issues identified: excessive dog waste (14 responses), public toilet cleaning (12 responses), playground equipment improvements (13 responses), and dog waste removal signage (10 responses). Updated concept design includes new irrigation system, shade structures, drinking fountain, retaining walls, and improved signage.

Report responding to Council request for draft plans and costing for Kiss and Drive facility on Dodd Street adjacent to Lake Monger Primary School. Proposes 12-month trial period for Kiss and Drive on Dodd Street west of Gregory Street and formalisation of existing pedestrian crossing point with safety improvements. Feedback from school included requests for increased capacity, angled parking, zebra crossing, mini-roundabout, and improved Gregory Street verge parking.

Final review of the Empire Park Freeplay Zone trial period. Report details activities throughout the trial, feedback from members of the public, hazards identified and actions completed to maintain site safety. 28 complaints received regarding unauthorised and anti-social behavioural activities including unauthorised excavations, furniture importation, lighting of fires, signage removal, litter, graffiti, track erosion, and flora damage. Aerial photos indicate minor changes in vegetation. Installation of conservation fence recommended to delineate the area and mitigate vegetation damage.

Blackspot funding application for Jersey Street and Grantham Street intersection. Study identified 31 crashes over five-year period (2017-2021), with over 80% involving right-turn movements. Four treatment options assessed: traffic signals, roundabout, restricted turn movements, and multi-intersection treatment. Main Roads Western Australia does not support traffic signals due to insufficient traffic volume warrants. Roundabout not feasible due to land constraints. Multi-intersection treatment submitted for Blackspot funding. Community consultation recommended on all options except roundabout.

Lake Monger Recreation Club upgrade project - Stage One detailed design and Stage Two concept design. Building identified as priority for disability access upgrades in 2019-2022 DAIP. Currently non-compliant with National Construction Code regarding accessible toilets, paths of travel, floor levels, doorways, and accessible parking. Design to be delivered in two stages to spread costs and minimise disruption. Feasibility study determined that constructing public UAT in isolation would be inefficient and expensive. Sewer connection required due to site being on septic system at capacity.

Review of 2018-2022 Cambridge Senior Services Strategy. Strategy endorsed by Council in May 2018 to support seniors (55+ years) to age in place. Review based on community consultation, attendance data and community profiling. Cambridge Senior Services Community Feedback and Satisfaction Survey conducted July-August 2022 with 44 responses showing 85-93% satisfaction with activities, outings and information sessions. Key achievement was establishment of Cambridge Seniors Hub at Wembley Community Centre. Census data shows seniors (60-85+) increased from 21.1% (2016) to 24% (2021) of Town's population.

Leederville Sporting Club lease variation. Club seeking to permanently incorporate area currently utilised under temporary licence agreement dated 23 November 2021 expiring 31 December 2022. Temporary licence area located between Youth Centre and Leederville Sporting Club. Fence relocated 7 February 2022. Community consultation undertaken via letter drop 3 February to 7 March 2022 (33 days) with informal feedback until 30 August 2022. Nine replies from seven residents received: one in support, eight objecting. Area has been activated as children's play area. Club experienced increased patronage requiring extra space.
