Draft amended Policy 3.3: Building Height addresses dormer windows and multiple dwelling height requirements. Proposed amendments include revised definition of dormer, exemption of dormers from building height calculation subject to specified conditions (width not exceeding 1.5 metres, height not exceeding half roof height, projection not exceeding 1.0 metre, location minimum 0.5 metres below ridge line and from outer wall, maximum one dormer per elevation), and deletion of reference to windows within roof. For multiple dwellings, new height requirements aligned with R-Codes, permitting three-storey developments in R60 areas and five-storey developments in R160 areas, with two-storey restriction for lower density codings up to R40.

Report on Empire Avenue shared path proposal between The Boulevard and Durston Road adjacent to Wembley Golf Course. Path length 2,530 metres, width 3 metres, proposed marigold concrete pavement. Estimated cost $500,000. Issues addressed: boundary road issues with City of Stirling (100% Town responsibility for path construction and maintenance on southern verge per existing agreement), priority of completing link between existing paths, hazards from golf ball strikes (five fairways identified with risk, netting costs estimated at minimum $100,000 per fairway for 200 metres), width and alignment considerations (3 metres preferred, 2.5 metres next preference, 2 metres minimum legal width, alignment adjacent to fence for most of route except 460 metres between Boulevard and Dumfries Road at 1 metre from kerb), verge landscaping impact with some replacement trees required near Tuscany Way and Valencia Avenue, and proposed roadworks coordination with roundabout construction at Empire Avenue/Durston Road intersection.

Report on Birkdale Street parking improvements presenting four design options (Option 1, Option 1A, Option 2, Option 3) to maximise parking provisions between Cambridge Street and Newry Street while addressing safety and amenity concerns. Option 1 selected after independent engineering consultant review by Porter Consulting Engineers. Existing parking 17 bays (west side 10, east side 7). Option 1 provides 24 bays total (increase of 7 bays all on west side). Option 1A concept extends design to Salvado Road with potential 21 bays on west side (increase of 12 bays). Options 2 and 3 rejected due to safety and amenity constraints including inadequate road width for safe manoeuvring, risk of corner cutting at intersection, inadequate footpath widths, and potential increased traffic conflict.

Bold Park Aquatic Centre Redevelopment - Pool Heating. Report addressing supplemental heating system requirements for outdoor 50m pool at Bold Park Aquatic Centre. Recent cold evenings caused pool to cool to sub-optimal temperatures of 23-24°C at opening despite existing heating system operating at full capacity. Design review determined approximately 400 kW peak heating capacity required during winter months to maintain 27°C operational temperature. Existing system comprises 93 panels of evacuated tube solar heating (approximately 170 kW) and 2 existing 200 kW heat pumps (20 years old, using R22 refrigerant). Remediation involves procuring tertiary heat pump system with 230 kW installed capacity. Pool heating contractor able to supply units within 7 days and commission within fortnight. Single source quotation of $81,000 for supply, installation and commissioning provided. Total estimated budget for tertiary heating system including electrical works is $120,000. Design team undertaking design and documentation at no cost.

Various amendments made to draft budget including Festivals and Events budget increase for Truck Stop Event, City Beach Commercial Precinct loan repayment correction, Corporate software budget reduction, rate modelling with 2.7% GR V rate increase, Parking budget revision, City Beach Tennis Club needs assessment adjustment, Perry Lakes lot sale profit adjustment, carry forward projects totalling $3.4 million, fees and charges amendments including cash in lieu for parking increases. Notional advice received that Department of Local Government and Communities grants may be reduced by $28,000 but not confirmed. 2015/2016 year-end results show small surplus expected, predominantly from road infrastructure project savings due to low asphalt costs from reduced oil prices.

Development Assessment Panels Discussion Paper - Report on the discussion paper 'Implementing Development Assessment Panels in Western Australia' released for public comment by Department of Planning. The paper proposes Local Development Assessment Panels (LDAPs) and Joint Development Assessment Panels (JDAPs) to determine certain prescribed class and value applications. Town of Cambridge would form part of West Metropolitan JDAP covering Cambridge, Claremont, Cottesloe, Mosman Park, Nedlands, Peppermint Grove and Subiaco. Report concludes the Town should not support the proposal in form presented, as it provides no benefit to Town, community or applicants and would strip Council of ability to implement decisions consistent with strategic direction. Only 1.6% of Town applications in 2008/09 were eligible for JDAP consideration, none having regional or State significance.

2012 Cambridge Library Biennial Community Survey. Survey conducted in September 2012 with 422 responses (highest to date and 355% higher than 2010 survey). Survey assessed patron satisfaction, usage patterns, borrowing materials, opening hours, and service development priorities. Results showed 53% rated library as excellent, 42% as very good, 99% would recommend to others. Key satisfaction areas: library environment (59% excellent), desk service quality (58%), staff assistance (54%), overall layout (46%).

Wembley Golf Course - Fee Review 2012. Annual review of fees at WGC benchmarked against nine other public golf courses in metropolitan area. Proposed marginal fee increases effective 1 January 2013 covering green fees, driving range, memberships, golf carts, hire clubs, teaching, and function room. Recommendation to implement new Super Seniors concession ($14-20 for 9-18 holes after 11am weekdays). New booking system to be installed December 2012. Further pricing review planned for June 2013.

Quarry Amphitheatre Concept Master Plan. Design review completed by Cox Howlett and Bailey Woodland with Graham Walne as Theatre Consultant. Concept Master Plan developed for staged approach maintaining connection to existing ambience. Key design elements address additional seating, new stage surface, improved lighting and power, off-stage storage, improved access from café to stage, new front of house facilities, control room, increased parking, disabled access compliance, and increased toilets. Overall cost approximately $6 million in three stages: Stage 1 ($1,150,000), Stage 1A ($2,000,000), Stage 2 ($2,850,000).

Wembley Golf Course Trail - Concept Plan. Concept design developed for staged development of trails within Wembley Golf Course. Trail features include predominantly asphalt sealed paths (2.5-3 metres width), natural contours where possible, suitable for walkers and cyclists, fencing to mitigate golf course access risk, connections to existing pedestrian paths, interpretative signage. Stage 1A: path from driving range to Empire Avenue near Newman College ($400,000-$450,000). Stage 1B: paths to Empire Avenue near Weaponess Road and Durston Avenue ($200,000-$220,000). Stage 1C: bush trail near potential wetlands ($125,000-$140,000).

Surf Club Building and Commercial Development at City Beach: Food and Beverage Operators. Responses to Expressions of Interest for food and beverage facility operations. 14 proposals received covering range of facilities with different size preferences. Confidential report by specialists reviewed proposals and identified preferred mix. Town advised previous decision to reduce commercial space to ~1,400m2 would result in only 3 facilities increasing project risk. Proposed process includes negotiation with preferred operators then public advertisement of proposed leases prior to Council appointment.

Review of the Structure for Crime Prevention in Western Australia. State Government released report on 18 October 2002 titled "New Structures for Crime Prevention in Western Australia". WALGA circulated Info Page on 25 October 2002 seeking feedback from member Councils. Report reviewed crime prevention structure to identify needs and priorities, determine effective delivery model, assess State Government agency involvement, and assess Local Government and community participation. Safer WA Western Suburbs Committee contributed through workshop on 15 May 2002. Review findings indicate Local Government has moved from interested observer to active employer of crime prevention staff. Local Government identified as most consistent partner in crime prevention collaborations with central role in promoting strategies. Particular involvement in Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) noted. Community consultation and participation identified as important characteristics for effective crime prevention. Broader Safer WA structure identified as not working well despite local-level success. Report examined degree to which Safer WA structure has assisted development of partnerships.

Review of Miscellaneous Fees and Charges 1997/98. Review of Respite and Children's Services Fees and Charges 1997/98. Report recommends static Day Centre fees ($8 per day), unchanged In Home Respite fees ($4 per hour), unchanged Occasional Care fees ($5 per hour). For Out of School Care, recommends Vacation Care weekly fee increase from $70 to $80, Getaways from $70 to $90 including excursions, unchanged daily fee of $20. Before and After School fees remain unchanged with removal of multi-child discounts.

Draft Local Planning Strategy - Report on Community Consultation. The Town prepared a draft Local Planning Strategy (LPS) to set out the long-term planning framework for the whole local government area. The draft LPS was advertised for comment between 20 August 2018 and 27 September 2018. Report presents feedback from consultation and seeks Council adoption of the draft LPS, subject to modifications, for submission to the Western Australian Planning Commission (WAPC) for certification.

Community consultation on Draft Local Planning Strategy occurred between 20 August 2018 and 27 September 2018 (later extended to 17 September 2018 per notice). Two information sessions held on 25 August 2018 (Boulevard, Floreat) and 8 September 2018 (Leederville Bowling Club, West Leederville) with total of 86 recorded attendees. Total of 537 submissions received (504 survey submissions, 9 emails, 24 letters). Communications and engagement mechanisms included flyers to all owners and occupiers, online and hardcopy surveys, Facebook posts, permanent display at Administration Building, notices in Post Newspaper, public notice on website, summary brochure, posters, FAQs, and letters to key service agencies.

Community submissions on Draft Local Planning Strategy analysed by topic. High level of support for Character and Heritage, Traffic and Transport, Community Infrastructure and Facilities, Natural Asset Management, Wembley Activity Centre, Housing, Economy and Employment, Public Realm and Open Space. Majority level of support for Utility and Service Infrastructure, West Leederville Activity Centre, Cambridge Street Urban Corridor, Ocean Village Neighbourhood Centre, Local Centres. Mixed level of support for Floreat Activity Centre and Gayton Road Neighbourhood Centre, Other Residential Development. 537 submissions analysed including qualitative and quantitative responses. Of 537 submissions, 144 provided identical or fundamentally the same responses. Late submissions from Floreat Primary School, DoE, Department of Communities, Department of Transport, Main Roads WA, Department of Water and Environment, Pindan and G.P.A Pty Ltd considered despite being submitted after closing date.

Draft Policy 2.7 - Design Review Panels. Report presents proposal to establish a Design Review Panel and seeks to define the scope and purpose through adoption of DRP Policy for public advertising. Design Review Panels to consist of qualified members from Architecture, Urban Design, Landscape Architecture, Sustainable Design, and Character Heritage Conservation. Certain classes of development will be referred to DRP including development exceeding $5 million, buildings three storeys or higher, residential development of ten or more dwellings, and non-residential development abutting residential zoned land.

Local Planning Policy 5.2 Advertising Signs - advertising process and public submission summary. Policy was advertised from 4 March 2016 to 4 April 2016 (extended to 31 days from standard 21 days to account for public holidays). Two advertisements in Cambridge Post, website notices, and letters to commercial property owners and ratepayer groups. Five submissions received objecting to the policy on grounds of unnecessary regulation and negative business impact. Main arguments were that there should be less control over advertising signage or no planning approval required. Policy modifications seek to clarify requirements, prohibit third-party advertising and large billboards, and exempt temporary and minor signs from approval.

Underground Power - Reconsideration of Round 6 Funding Applications. Updated advice from Department of Finance requires revised proposal areas to comply with SUPP guidelines of 500-800 lots and 93% residential minimum. Scheme Amendment No.31 to Town Planning Scheme No.1 - Minister of Planning Modifications and Readvertising. The Town was notified on 7 April 2016 that the Minister for Planning directed Council to modify and readvertise Town Planning Scheme Amendment 31. The modified amendment involves significantly altered proposals including corner lot density bonus, split coding for grouped/multiple dwellings, Cambridge Street split-coding R40/R60, removal of Manor House Apartment option, and deletion of Additional Uses clause. When modelled, the development potential reduces from 2363 dwellings to approximately 2145 dwellings. The Town must readvertise for 60 days and make a recommendation to the Minister by December 2016.

Herdsman Main Drain Stormwater - Potential Reuse Project. Report on findings from initial study regarding potential reuse of stormwater flowing in the Herdsman Main Drain to ocean outfall. Study investigated feasibility of diverting water to Wembley Golf Course for aquifer replenishment, infiltration basin creation, injection bores, main dam offset, or feature lakes. Most preferred option identified as gravity-fed infiltration basin (~$960,000 capital, $125,000 annual operating costs) to infiltrate approximately 2GL per annum into aquifer, addressing water supply sustainability in drying climate and maintaining groundwater extraction licenses.

Comprehensive report on the redevelopment of Perry Lakes Stadium Site alternative development strategy approved in-principle at Special Council Meeting of 18 May 2005. Report addresses the process and requirements to effect the proposal including Business Plan requirements, Request for Tender implications, State Government response, sporting stakeholder views, UWA negotiations, preliminary financial analysis, planning outcomes, and implementation requirements. Perry Lakes Aquifer Replenishment Project. Federal Government grant of $2.589 million secured for capital works. Project involves infiltration of treated wastewater into underground galleries at Perry Lakes to replenish aquifer. CSIRO-based research. State Government offers marginal financial support: Department of Water $85,000 per year for three years for monitoring; Landcorp $110,000 over two years for operating costs. Annual Town operating costs estimated $200,000-$240,000 after initial subsidy period. Approximately 15 trees require removal for gallery installation. Approval required with conditions including State Government payment binding undertakings, cost limits, and Water Corporation supply agreement with termination right for Town.

South City Beach Kiosk progress report. Kiosk constructed 1970, concrete formwork construction. Listed as Category 2 building in Local Government Heritage inventory 2018. Operated by lessees until October 2013. Public toilets and change rooms closed 2015 due to structural integrity concerns. Spalling of concrete soffit continued to worsen due to corrosion of steel reinforcement in aggressive coastal environment. Structural condition survey undertaken June 2016 by Peritas Group, report presented to Council November 2016.

South City Beach Kiosk - community consultation 2017. Following community consultation in September 2017, 91% of 1,360 respondents elected for building to be retained. Ordinary Council Meeting December 2017 (CR17.183) resolved: building to be retained; public toilets part remains closed available as floor space for future use; expressions of interest sought February/March 2018 for proposals to operate building; Town prepares proposal for community use beach shelter/barbecues area; no major investment in repairing soffit until Council determines nature and timing of new use.

South City Beach Kiosk - structural assessment 2019. Structural condition assessment undertaken by Alliance Engineering Consultants (AEC) on 17 June 2019. Report identified significant remedial works required to repair concrete structure. Key findings: area with significant structural damage is slab soffit exposed to environment; concrete degradation due to corrosion of reinforcement steel has occurred; corrosion of bars very advanced, unlikely all affected bars can be treated, affected bars to be removed and replaced.

South City Beach Kiosk - Council Forum February 2020. Council Forum held 11 February 2020 to discuss future of Kiosk and amenities. Six options tabled: (1) Do nothing - building will deteriorate to point of demolition necessity; (2) Demolish facility ~$20,000; (3) Repair roof to serviceable standard ~$300,000-$400,000; (4) Repair roof and refurbish for original use ~$675,000; (5) Demolish and rebuild with similar architectural design for community use; (6) Community consultation - let community decide based on costs and condition.
